problems.title: Coverage needs growth of every relevant fibre
problems.source_location: Appendix D, Theorem D.3, p. 28; Remark D.4, pp. 28–29.
claim: Appendix D extends coverage to arbitrary coordinate subsets and factor domains, beyond its finite union bound.
analysis: Full-tuple coverage fails for a proper training subset when \(k=n\). Even with \(k<n\), domains \([N]\times[2]\), sample fraction \(1/2\) and \(k=1\) have probability \(2^N/\binom{2N}{N}\to0\) of seeing every first-coordinate value. There are only two completions per such value, so overall dataset growth does not make its fibre large.
result: The finite avoidance/union bound survives; the general asymptotic coverage implication needs fibre assumptions.
assumptions: Only the cited paper version and explicitly described mathematical or implementation conditions are assessed.
repair: For a coordinate set \(A\), use fibre size \(M/N_A\) and exact avoidance probability \(\binom{M-M/N_A}{m}/\binom{M}{m}\). Require the resulting union bound to vanish rather than only total domain size to grow.
problems.impact_rationale: This limits a supporting coverage extension; successful reconstruction is not independently refuted.
problems.existing_correction_status: An explicit local correction is described; author adoption and a corresponding published erratum are not established.

problems.title: A final constraint can exclude a prefix allowed by the average constraint
claim: Proposition E.1 claims prefix-set inclusion for arbitrary positive average and final reconstruction thresholds.
analysis: Use one input, teacher message \(00\), and two-bit alternatives. Both one-bit receiver outputs are \(0\); complete messages \(00,01\) reconstruct \(0\), while \(10,11\) reconstruct \(0.15\). Sender \(10\) has average discrepancy \(0.075<0.1\), yet its prefix \(1\) has no completion below final threshold \(0.1\).
result: Arbitrary-threshold prefix inclusion is false. Nonnegative loss still bounds final discrepancy by the number of positions times the average.
assumptions: Only the cited paper version and explicitly described mathematical or implementation conditions are assessed.
repair: Use the valid relation that average threshold \(M\) implies final threshold \(CM\) for message length \(C\), or impose additional receiver/threshold structure before asserting stronger inclusion.
problems.impact_rationale: This is a local feasible-set proposition, not a direct failure of the learned communication system.
problems.existing_correction_status: An explicit local correction is described; author adoption and a corresponding published erratum are not established.

problems.title: Codeword length is not the description of an arbitrary encoder
problems.source_location: Definition F.2 and Eqs. (10)–(12), p. 31; Proposition F.3.
claim: Equation (11) assigns encoding complexity approximately \(\sum_i\log_2N_i\), while Definition F.2 permits arbitrary injective factor encoders of minimal codeword length.
analysis: For two factors of size \(N=2^m\), a minimal-length injective encoder is a permutation of \(N\) codewords. There are \((N!)^2\) compositional maps. Counting descriptions forces typical map complexity of order \(N\log N\), not the \(2\log_2N\) bits in one encoded factor pair. A half-domain containing each factor value can still distinguish the maps. A fixed simple rule-based encoder is an important restricted alternative, but its simplicity is not implied by injectivity.
result: The universal encoder-description comparison omits the allowed function class and conditioning context.
assumptions: The encoder class includes arbitrary injective minimal-codeword factor maps; no fixed external encoder description is supplied for free.
repair: Distinguish message length, encoder description and conditional description given a fixed encoder. Restrict to a specified simple encoder family before using a logarithmic map-complexity denominator.
problems.impact_rationale: This is a fundamental counting failure in the central compressive-description justification.
problems.existing_correction_status: An explicit local correction is described; author adoption and a corresponding published erratum are not established.

problems.title: The contrastive upper bound fails in the exact one-hot regime
claim: Equation (32) bounds the nonnegative self-positive contrastive loss by \(-1+N-\log N-\bar d\).
analysis: For \(N=2\) identical exact-one-hot messages, true loss is \(\log2\approx0.69315\), while the claimed upper bound is \(1-\log2\approx0.30685\). Distinct binary messages give true loss \(\log(1+e^{-1})\approx0.31326\), but claimed bound approximately \(-0.19315\). Both satisfy the exact message regime, so a negative bound cannot upper-bound this positive loss.
result: The algebraic bound cited to support the PDM connection is false. This does not assert that the reported large-batch experiment used this small batch.
assumptions: The claimed bound is general in batch size and applies to exact one-hot messages at unit temperature.
repair: Retain the exact log-sum-exp expression or supply a valid inequality with its normalization and diagonal terms. No replacement empirical objective is validated.
problems.impact_rationale: The derivation has a glaring sign/scale contradiction in a claimed general bound linked to the main objective.
problems.existing_correction_status: An explicit local correction is described; author adoption and a corresponding published erratum are not established.

problems.title: The soft PDM implementation uses norm-weighted averaging
problems.source_location: Eq.(3), PDF p.6; author release losses.py, pdm, lines 42–56
claim: Equation (3) averages positionwise cosines; `losses.py`, `pdm`, instead divides a sum of dot products by a sum of norm products.
analysis: For positive two-symbol rows \((0.9,0.1),(0.5,0.5)\) against \((0.9,0.1),(0.9,0.1)\), the release yields approximately \(0.903916\), while the mean cosine is \(0.890434\). Equal-norm and one-hot messages are passing cases. The hard branch additionally uses a count rather than a fraction at fixed length.
result: The soft release objective differs from the defined mean. Historical experiment code is unresolved.
assumptions: Only the cited paper version and explicitly described mathematical or implementation conditions are assessed.
repair: Normalize each position’s dot product before averaging. State any deliberate hard-branch length scaling and corresponding objective coefficient.
problems.impact_rationale: This is a release objective mismatch, with no established central experimental effect.
problems.existing_correction_status: An explicit local correction is described; author adoption and a corresponding published erratum are not established.

problems.title: Convex loss need not give a unique reconstruction
claim: Appendix G.3 infers uniqueness of the optimal deterministic reconstruction from convexity.
analysis: For conditional \(X=\pm1\) with equal probabilities and absolute reconstruction loss, every \(y\in[-1,1]\) has risk \(1\). Convexity gives no uniqueness. Squared Euclidean loss instead has the unique conditional mean under a finite second moment.
result: The universal uniqueness inference fails; the squared-error experiments are unaffected by this example.
assumptions: Only the cited paper version and explicitly described mathematical or implementation conditions are assessed.
repair: Require an appropriate strict-convexity condition, or state existence/optimality without uniqueness.
problems.impact_rationale: This is a generality qualification outside the unaffected squared-error special case.
problems.existing_correction_status: An explicit local correction is described; author adoption and a corresponding published erratum are not established.
